0.long_answer: The famous amnesia patient is Henry Molaison, commonly referred to as H.M. He underwent an experimental surgery in 1953 in which his bilateral medial temporal lobes were removed to alleviate his severe epilepsy. As a result of this surgery, he experienced profound anterograde amnesia, which is the inability to form new memories, as well as retrograde amnesia, which affected memories from the period just before the operation. His case has been extensively studied in neuroscience and psychology and contributed significantly to our understanding of the role of the medial temporal lobes, including the hippocampus, in memory formation and retrieval.
